topics.label: Introduction to cancer causation and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, outlines the learning outcomes, and frames the six-lecture series on the causes of cancer.

topics.label: Conceptual frameworks of cancer etiology: genetics, endogenous processes, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the broad principles driving cancer initiation, including the debate over random endogenous mutations versus environmental exposures and geographic epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Biological, chemical, and promotional mechanisms of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail specific agents and mechanisms that cause cancer, spanning viral oncogenesis, dietary and chemical mutagens, metabolic bioactivation, chronic inflammation, and tumor promotion.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the experimental, genomic, and epidemiological methods used to detect carcinogen exposure and evaluate mutagenic potential.
